name: Mix Veg Curry

ingredients.name: Potato (aloo)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ small potato, peeled, cut into 1.5 cm cubes (about ⅓ cup)

ingredients.name: Carrot (gajar)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ medium carrot, cut into 1 cm cubes (about ¼ cup)

ingredients.name: French beans (farasbi)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 5–6 beans, cut into 2 cm pieces (about ¼ cup)

ingredients.name: Capsicum (shimla mirch), green
ingredients.householdMeasure: ¼ medium capsicum, cut into 2 cm squares

ingredients.name: Onion (pyaz/kanda)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ medium onion, finely chopped (about ⅓ cup)

ingredients.name: Tomato (tamatar)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1 medium ripe tomato, finely chopped (about ½ cup)

ingredients.name: Green chilli (hari mirch)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ small chilli, slit or chopped

equipment: Chopping board, knife and vegetable peeler (no peeler? scrape the potato and carrot with the back of the knife or peel thinly with the knife)
Kadai or medium heavy pan with a lid (about 20 cm)
Mortar and pestle (khalbatta) or grater for the ginger and garlic
Measuring spoons and a measuring cup (a normal teaspoon and a steel glass are fine stand-ins)
Small bowl of water, for the splash in step 14

steps.title: Wash the vegetables
steps.text: Rinse the potato, carrot, beans, cauliflower florets and capsicum under running water.
steps.tip: Soak cauliflower florets 5 min in warm salted water if you see small worms or dirt in the folds.
steps.visualCue: No soil on the potato or carrot; florets clean
steps.cameraCheck: The washed vegetables on the board
steps.videoShot: Vegetables rinsed in a colander under the tap.

steps.title: Cut the potato
steps.text: Peel ½ small potato (50 g) and cut it into 1.5 cm cubes. Keep the cubes in a little water.
steps.tip: Small cubes matter; big ones stay hard when the rest is done.
steps.visualCue: Even, small cubes, about ⅓ cup
steps.videoShot: A knife cubing a peeled potato.

steps.title: Cut the carrot
steps.text: Peel ½ medium carrot (40 g) and cut it into 1 cm cubes.
steps.visualCue: Small orange cubes, slightly smaller than the potato
steps.videoShot: Carrot being diced.

steps.title: Cut the beans
steps.text: Top and tail 5–6 French beans (30 g) and cut them into 2 cm pieces.
steps.visualCue: Short green pieces, about ¼ cup
steps.videoShot: A bunch of beans cut across in one go.

steps.title: Cut the cauliflower
steps.text: Break or cut 50 g cauliflower into 4–5 small florets, about 2.5 cm across.
steps.visualCue: Small, even florets
steps.videoShot: A knife splitting florets.

steps.title: Cut the capsicum
steps.text: Cut ¼ capsicum (25 g) into 2 cm squares; keep it separate (it goes in last).
steps.visualCue: Green squares, seeds removed
steps.cameraCheck: The capsicum squares in their own bowl
steps.videoShot: Capsicum cut into squares.

steps.title: Measure the peas
steps.text: Measure 3 tbsp (30 g) green peas; if frozen, rinse them in a sieve.
steps.visualCue: Bright green peas, no ice
steps.videoShot: Peas poured into a bowl.

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.text: Finely chop ½ medium onion (60 g).
steps.visualCue: Small, even pieces, about ⅓ cup
steps.videoShot: Knife chopping onion finely.

steps.title: Chop the tomato
steps.text: Finely chop 1 medium ripe tomato (90 g).
steps.visualCue: Small red pieces with their juice, about ½ cup
steps.videoShot: Tomato chopped on the board.

steps.title: Crush the aromatics
steps.text: Crush or grate ½-inch ginger (3 g) and 2 small garlic cloves (4 g); slit ½ small green chilli (2 g).
steps.visualCue: Coarse paste, strong smell
steps.videoShot: Ginger and garlic pounded in a khalbatta.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Put the kadai on medium heat with 2 tsp (10 g) oil.
steps.visualCue: Oil shimmers and flows easily
steps.videoShot: Oil swirled in a hot kadai.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Add ¼ tsp cumin seeds and 1 bay leaf.
steps.tip: If the cumin turns black at once, the oil is too hot; lower the heat.
steps.visualCue: Cumin sizzles and darkens one shade; nutty smell
steps.videoShot: Cumin crackling in oil.

steps.title: Cook the onion
steps.text: Add the onion and stir often on medium heat.
steps.visualCue: Soft and light golden at the edges, sweet smell, no raw sharpness
steps.videoShot: Onion stirred as it turns golden.

steps.title: Add the aromatics and powders
steps.text: Add the ginger-garlic and green chilli, stir 1 min, then lower the heat and add a pinch of turmeric, ½ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder and ¾ tsp coriander powder with 1 tbsp water. Stir.
steps.tip: The splash of water stops the powders from burning.
steps.visualCue: Raw garlic smell gone; spices smell toasted, not burnt; masala turns orange
steps.videoShot: Powders sprinkled in, a splash of water hissing.

steps.title: Cook the tomato
steps.text: Add the tomato and ⅓ tsp (2 g) salt. Cook on medium, stirring and mashing with the spoon.
steps.visualCue: Tomato breaks down into a thick, jammy masala and oil shows at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: The oil at the edge of the masala
steps.videoShot: Spoon mashing tomato in the kadai.

steps.title: Add the slow vegetables
steps.text: Drain the potato and add it with the carrot and cauliflower. Stir to coat them in the masala.
steps.visualCue: Every piece coated orange
steps.videoShot: Vegetables tossed in masala.

steps.title: Add beans, peas and water
steps.text: Add the beans, peas and 120 ml (½ cup) water. Stir and bring to a boil.
steps.visualCue: Gravy bubbling around the vegetables
steps.videoShot: Water poured in and the pan coming to a boil.

steps.title: Simmer covered
steps.text: Cover and simmer on low, stirring once halfway.
steps.tip: If it dries out, add 2–3 tbsp hot water.
steps.visualCue: Potato and carrot almost soft; gravy thicker
steps.cameraCheck: The pan with the lid lifted
steps.videoShot: Steam rising as the lid comes off.

steps.title: Add the capsicum
steps.text: Add the capsicum and cook uncovered on medium.
steps.visualCue: Capsicum bright green and just tender; gravy coats the vegetables
steps.videoShot: Capsicum squares stirred in.

steps.title: Check doneness
steps.text: Press a potato cube and a carrot cube with the spoon.
steps.tip: Still hard? Cover and cook 2–3 min more with a splash of water.
steps.visualCue: Both crush easily; beans tender but still green
steps.cameraCheck: A crushed potato cube on the spoon
steps.videoShot: Spoon pressing a potato cube.

steps.title: Finish with garam masala and kasuri methi
steps.text: Sprinkle ¼ tsp garam masala and crush ½ tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the pan. Stir and turn off the heat.
steps.visualCue: Green flecks, warm smell
steps.cameraCheck: The kasuri methi on the curry
steps.videoShot: Palms rubbing kasuri methi over the pan.

steps.title: Taste and adjust
steps.text: Taste; add a pinch of salt only if needed, or 2 tbsp hot water for more gravy.
steps.visualCue: Savoury, mildly spicy, tangy from tomato
steps.videoShot: A spoonful lifted for tasting.

steps.title: Garnish and serve
steps.text: Remove the bay leaf, transfer to a bowl and scatter 1 tsp chopped coriander leaves on top.
steps.visualCue: Colourful vegetables (orange, green, white, yellow) in a thick orange-red gravy
steps.videoShot: Coriander scattered over the bowl, steam rising.

reasons: about 225 g of six different vegetables per bowl, about 9.5 g fibre, good vitamin A, C and K and potassium, only 2 tsp oil, no frying, no added sugar, no saturated-fat-heavy dairy and no cholesterol, at about 255 kcal. Points off for low protein (about 7 g, so it needs dal, curd or paneer alongside) and moderate sodium (about 850 mg). Restaurant versions often fry the vegetables first and add butter, cream, cashew paste or paneer, with 2–3 times the oil, so 400–550 kcal bowls with 10 g or more saturated fat are common.

researchRating.basis: a staple, widely cooked and well-reviewed everyday curry: Hebbar's Kitchen's mix veg curry shows 4.97 from 372 votes, Veg Recipes of India's one-pot mix veg 4.95 from about 58–60 votes (with at least 2 pages of comments) and its mix veg gravy 4.88 from 25 votes, and almost every major Indian recipe site (Tarla Dalal, Ranveer Brar, Jeyashri's Kitchen, Subbu's Kitchen, Indian Healthy Recipes) publishes it; it is on nearly every pure-veg restaurant menu. Points off because it is seen as a plain, "safe" or leftover-vegetable dish rather than a favourite, and restaurant versions are often described as generic. Platform dish ratings were not used.

storage: Fridge-safe in a closed box for up to 2 days (cool within 1 hour); Veg Recipes of India also gives 1–2 days. Freezer: possible for up to 1 month, but potato turns grainy and capsicum soft; better to freeze a batch without potato. Reheat in a pan on low with 2–3 tbsp water, stirring, until it bubbles; or microwave in 1-minute bursts, stirring between.
leftoverRemix: Mix veg paratha or veg frankie. Cook the leftover curry down until dry, mash it lightly with a fork, add 1 tbsp chopped coriander and a pinch of chaat masala, then stuff it into atta dough for parathas, or roll it in a warm roti with sliced onion and green chutney and toast it on a tawa with ½ tsp oil.
burnOff: about 3.6 km of running (255 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 5.1 km of brisk walking (about 1 h at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With 2 phulkas (about 435 kcal): about 6.2 km running or 8.7 km walking (est.).

navratri.reason: onion, garlic, green peas, French beans and cauliflower are outside the common vrat rule set; a vrat sabzi of potato, raw banana or pumpkin with sendha namak is a different dish.

ekadashi.reason: no grains; skip the green peas and French beans (legumes) and the onion and garlic (common rule set; family rules on vegetables and spices vary).

jain.reason: potato, carrot, onion, garlic and fresh ginger are root vegetables; use the Jain variant (raw banana, beans, peas, cauliflower, capsicum, tomato; sonth).

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; a light, high-fibre curry with roti for iftar dinner or sehri; moderate salt (about 850 mg sodium), so go easy on extra salt before a fast.

jain.reason: potato, carrot, onion, garlic and fresh ginger are root vegetables; drop all five, use raw banana for potato, more beans and peas for carrot, and dry ginger powder (sonth) (see Jain variant).

vegan.reason: vegetables, oil and spices only; no ghee, butter, curd, paneer or cream in the main recipe.

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, no meat, so it fits a pescatarian diet.

sattvik.reason: skip onion and garlic and build the gravy on tomato and ginger (see Sattvik variant).

glutenFree.reason: no wheat, maida, rava or besan, and the main recipe uses no hing; if you add hing, use a gluten-free one, as most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour. Check the garam masala label for added flour.

dairyFree.reason: no dairy in the main recipe (restaurant versions often add cream, butter or paneer; ask when ordering).
